title: The value graph lets you add points, pick the segments between them and change their easing
goal: Editing a property's graph (scale, opacity, position, tilt and the rest) should be direct: click the line to add a point there, click the segment between two points to pick it, right-click a segment to change its easing (or drag its handles), and drag points to change time and value. It works the same for every property.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-12): "I don't really see the point of adding a 3d pane just to show the rotation values. I think when we move or change transitions, we can show a small toolbar like overlay which shows the transform values for typing things in. But doing some other operation or changing the tool makes the transform overlay disappear. On the overlay there should be a reset button to reset to defaults. Also similarly, for when I have a keyframe and click the opacity dot, I want the same overlay to appear to tweak the opacity. Also editing the graph of a particular item like scale is really hard. I can right click on the scale, say show graph, but then when the graph is there, how do I add points on it? I click on the line, doesn't add a point, i can select a point but then if I have 2 points, I can't select the line in between. I want to be able to easily create nice transitions by adding points, selecting the segments between them, right clicking and changing their easing, etc. I need the ia to be consistent across the properties. When I add a 'key' to a video, it adds all of the animatable properties below it. I really wish there was a more scalable solution to the ux here, because we really should only show the properties being animated. And, if we want to clear one of them, i should be able to select one of the rows and hit delete to remove the whole property from being animated. but there should be a way to add it back. like maybe the keyframe line should be selectable and right clicked to animate a variety of things. or I can click it, tweak something (like transform) and the options are automatically added to that keyframe."

Five tasks, in order: the design (mocks), then the transform overlay, the key value overlay, the graph editor, and only-animated-properties with auto-key. Code pointers (read, not run): the 3D section is Space3DInspector (Sources/Photonz/Space3DInspector.swift, shown at InspectorPanel.swift:1526) with EditorState+Space3D.swift; key lanes and the graph toggle are KeyLanesView.swift (segments at :270, lane menus :156, :213, :423) and EditorState+KeyLanes.swift (:283 'Show Graph'); Add Key on a clip is EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift:199 and per property EditorState+PropertyKeys.swift:177 addKeyHere; the property strip is MotionStripView.swift. The shared curve list is EasingCurve (PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift) with Draw a Curve, and CurveRow from every-transition-can-be-picked-from-presets-and. Memory rules: one purpose per area (the IA contract in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md decides placement), mocks are the floor, legible text, no em dashes in UI copy. This is step 4 of 5.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: open Show Graph on scale and opacity, try clicking the line, picking a segment between two points, and changing easing; record what works in the audit
Click on the graph line (not on a point) adds a key at that time with the value the line has there, one undo step; Option-click adds without changing the curve shape

Segments between two keys are hit-testable and pickable (hover highlights the segment; click picks it; Shift adds); a picked segment shows its bezier handles, which can be dragged to shape the ease; right-click a segment (or a key, or several) offers the shared curve list, Draw a Curve, Linear, Hold (step) and Copy/Paste Ease
Dragging a point moves it in time and value with snapping to frames and to other keys, Shift locks to one axis; Delete removes picked points

The same interaction table for every property (position X/Y graphs separately or combined as the mock says, scale, rotation, opacity, tilt, depth, colour channels, blur); the graph auto-fits its value range with a way to zoom it
The graph is readable: value axis labels in the property's units, the playhead line through it, and the key overlay from the companion task opens from a point
A walk adds two scale keys, clicks the line between to add a third, picks a segment, sets Ease Out from its right-click, and checks the values at three moments
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
